'''Samuel Sanford Shapiro''' (July 13, 1930 – November 5, 2023) was an American [[Statistics|statistician]] and engineer. He was a professor emeritus of statistics at [[Florida International University]]. He was known for his co-authorship of the [[Shapiro–Wilk test]] and the [[Shapiro–Francia test]].

A native of [[New York City]], Shapiro graduated from [[City College of New York]] with a degree in statistics in 1952, and took an MS in industrial engineering at Columbia University in 1954. He briefly served as a statistician in the [[US Army]] [[Chemical Corps]], before earning a MS (1960) and PhD (1963) in statistics at [[Rutgers University]]. In 1972 he joined the faculty at Florida International University.

In 1987 he was elected a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm View/Search Fellows of the ASA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, accessed 2016-11-01.</ref>

Shapiro died on November 5, 2023, at the age of 93.<ref>{{cite web |title=Samuel S. Shapiro |url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/en-ca/obituaries/miami-fl/samuel-shapiro-11527069 |website=Dignity Memorial |access-date=28 December 2023}}</ref>
